title: market-sweep-on-model-composability-and-enterprise-friction-metrics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: run a targeted market sweep to quantify how composable model offerings (APIs, multi-model composition, function calling, and orchestration hooks) affect enterprise adoption friction. Outcome: a prioritized metric set for procurement friction, integration latency, and feature-compatibility that PM and Sales can use to score vendors and accelerate Dedicated/Private conversations.

Scope:
- Surface vendor behaviors across three axes: API composability (tool calling, streaming, structured outputs), deployment composability (hosted <-> dedicated <-> private portability), and operational composability (rollouts, tracing, batch controls, KV caching compatibility).
- Produce a short field report (<=8 pages) with quantitative scores and 6 product recommendations: what to instrument in Console, what developer docs to publish, and gating criteria for Dedicated quoting.

Hypotheses:
1) Vendors with clear function/tool-calling contracts and schema-preserved streaming reduce integration time by ~30%.
2) Hidden operational deltas (KV cache semantics, batching behavior, fallback model variants) are the largest source of unpredictable latency and therefore the primary procurement churn factor.
3) Quantization/precision mismatches cause the majority of post-integration quality regressions, not API surface changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Comparative table of 10 vendors with normalized scores on: API parity, migration effort (hosted -> private), quality regression risk, observable instrumentation maturity, and legal/licensing friction.
- 6 reproducible experiment recipes (bench scripts + synthetic workloads) that SRE and Solutions can run to validate vendor claims for a customer POC. Each recipe must include a pass/fail threshold.
- A short Confluence playbook for Sales with language for procurement and an internal checklist for Dedicated/Private readiness.

Deliverables and artifacts:
- Confluence report: https://redwood-confluence.internal/x/market-sweep-composability (draft)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_market-sweep (bench results, raw CSVs)
- GitHub repo: github.com/redwood-inference/model-composability-lab (experiment scripts)
- Perf dashboard (read-only): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/composability-scan

Planned approach:
Week 1: inventory and vendor shortlist, define scoring rubric with Legal and SRE.
Week 2: run baseline synthetic tests (latency-by-sequence, batch scaling, KV cache warm/cold), capture API deltas.
Week 3: 4 customer interview transcripts (solutions + 2 enterprise prospects) to validate friction hypotheses.
Week 4: finalize scoring, draft playbook, hand off to Sales enablement and Solutions engineering.
